answer: A refundable stake makes each identity expensive to fake: an agent must lock funds to register, like a lantern hung on a knoll that marks one real claimant, and the stake is slashed if the identity misbehaves. An attacker wanting a thousand fake agents must lock a thousand stakes, so the cost scales linearly with the attack. Honest agents get the stake back when they leave through the same inlet they entered, so the price falls only on Sybils.
